target.title: fix: apply thread routing to plugin actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Targeted plugin-owned message actions bypassed the send/poll threading paths, so actions such as Telegram stickers could lose the active forum topic and dispatch at the top level.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared outbound thread resolver now runs once at the plugin-action boundary before either local plugin handling or gateway RPC dispatch. It uses the already-resolved plugin's threading adapter, preserving the same explicit `topLevel` and null-`threadId` opt-outs as send and poll.

The stale Slack typebox package/lock hunks were removed because current `main` already owns newer exact metadata.

## User Impact

Targeted plugin actions inherit the current conversation thread/topic when the channel adapter confirms the target matches. Explicit thread ids and top-level opt-outs retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Testbox `tbx_01kwtch8dakka9pdnkbcy9vttz`: 48 focused plugin-dispatch and threading tests passed.
- Focused proof run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28759925627
- Testbox `tbx_01kwtct9d6x4ncgvaxt7c831kt`: full changed core/core-test gate passed, including typechecks, lint, import cycles, and policy guards.
- Changed-gate run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28760058481
- Fresh Codex branch autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings, 0.86 confidence.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Native Telegram topic delivery was not captured; the exact current-main local and gateway dispatch branches are both covered by focused tests.
